brief: A habit tracker as a garden — daily completion waters plants, streaks bloom, neglect wilts

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor mapping: seedling→bloom→wilt naturally encodes streak length, making progress feel emotional rather than numerical
Garden plot grid creates clear scannable structure with consistent flower anatomy reading as a unified visual system
Stat bar grounds the playful metaphor with concrete accountability numbers, balancing whimsy and utility
dominant_weaknesses: Flowers look like geometric primitives (circle + two leaves) rather than crafted illustration — feels like a wireframe of the idea, not the final art
Streak day-count pills overlap and crowd the habit-name labels, breaking the tidy plot frame and creating awkward typographic collisions
Blue gradient sky plus uniform brown plots is monotonous; no time-of-day, season, or weather variation despite the 'Perfect Growing Weather' chip promising it
fix_priorities: Redraw plant assets with real botanical variety per habit so each plot feels distinct, not eight clones of one flower
Fix label/streak-pill collision: integrate them into a single header strip inside or above the plot
Activate the weather/sky system — let it actually shift lighting, particles, or soil tone to reward the metaphor
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral charm leads, behavioral signaling (bloom vs wilt) is legible but coarse, and reflective payoff is shallow without history or seasonal arcs.
rationale.intent_fit: It executes the core garden metaphor competently but stops at the obvious literal mapping rather than pushing watering, weather, or wilt into a living system.
